items.title: Inbox: Louisville Athletics has partnered with a cryptocurrency company.
items.author: Matt Norlander
items.body_excerpt: Inbox: Louisville Athletics has partnered with a cryptocurrency company.

images.alt:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. – Louisville Athletics announced today a multi-year partnership with Ripple, the leading provider of blockchain-based enterprise solutions across traditional and digital finance, bringing XRP branding to Louisville Basketball beginning this season. 

 

XRP is a cryptocurrency that's fast, credible and efficient. In use since 2012 and trusted by institutions worldwide, XRP was developed to move money around the world in seconds, at a fraction of the cost of traditional banking.

 

As part of the agreement, the XRP logo becomes a permanent fixture on Denny Crum Court for every Louisville home game — preserving the court's history alongside XRP branding across Louisville Men's and Women's Basketball. Coach Crum’s iconic insignia will remain a permanent fixture on the playing surface inside the 3-point arc.

 

“Ripple was very intentional about aligning with premier basketball brands, and we’re proud

that Louisville was one of the programs they identified,” said Vice President and Director of

Athletics Josh Heird. “That speaks to the strength of our basketball tradition, the national reach

of the Louisville brand and the passion of our fan base. As college athletics continues to evolve,

we want to align with partners who recognize the value of what Louisville represents while

respecting the history that helped build it. This partnership does both, and I’m especially proud

that we’re able to move forward in a new and innovative way while continuing to honor Coach

Crum and the legacy of Denny Crum Court.”

images.alt: om Haberstroh and I considered several different options when we discussed the fifth spot on the ballot on a recent episode of The Big Number. Advanced numbers like EPM, LEBRON, DARKO, VORP and PER point toward Kawhi Leonard; he's top-five in all of them and has been sensational in shepherding the Clippers' gargantuan turnaround following their disastrous 6-21 start. He's averaging a career-high 28 points per game on 50/39/89 shooting, leading the NBA in points per touch (minimum 50 games played) while being just off the league lead in steals and just outside the top 10 in deflections; the Clippers have the point differential of a 59-win team when he's on the court, and have won at a 47-win pace (37-27) with him in the lineup.
